description.narrative: Bangladesh lies along the Ganges-Brahmaputra Delta, Asia’s largest and the world’s most densely populated delta. As per SRDI, over 30% of the cultivable area of Bangladesh lies in the coastal and offshore zones, with the area under salinity increasing year on year due to rising sea levels - from 0.83 million hectares to 1.056 million hectares over 36 years (in 2010). The severity of this situation is reflected in the prediction by scientists that food production in Bangladesh will decline by 50% in the coming decades. Coupled with the fact that more than 35 million people live in the coastal belt of Bangladesh, salinization exposes a huge proportion of vulnerable farmers to risks from climate change related challenges. Per day an average of 2.000 hectares of production land is lost to salinization and a total of 62 million hectares of agricultural land, an area 18 times the size of the Netherlands, has been affected by salinization. Climate change has exacerbated this further. Rising sea levels, more frequent and longer drought periods, scarcity of fresh water and large amounts of shallow saline groundwater have caused more salt to accumulate in the soil than the rain could wash out. The worst affected countries and regions in the world are Central Asia, Pakistan, and Bangladesh. Based on ICCO’s previous Research and Development project Saline Tolerant Agriculture in Bangladesh (STAB), and the Food Security and nutrition project- The Salt Solution (TSS), ICCO identified the needs and gaps to be worked through a new scale-up project like making salt-tolerant seeds and saline agriculture technologies, available for the coastal salinity affected farmers, enabling environment for extension of saline agriculture, strengthening local level output aggregation and marketing system etc.

Target Beneficiaries are Coastal Salinity affected farmers/ people in Bangladesh 1. 10000 Direct and 20000 Indirect farmers 2. 40 Farm Business Advisors (local entrepreneurs) 3. 16 Nursery Owners, 4. 16 Collection Point Management Committees

The goal of this project is “By 2024, 5000 hectares of coastal fallow land in Southern Bangladesh is sustainably utilized for diverse local food production and consumption”. Project objective is to support 10,000 farmers (of which 50% women) to transform 5,000 hectares of fallow land into productive agricultural land by introducing saline agriculture farming practices.
